newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU FLAT, SEEN STABLE ON LARGER DLR INFLOW.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU FLAT, SEEN STABLE ON LARGER DLR INFLOW.

text.p: Romania's leu closed the week stable as the central bank soaked up excess hard currencies generated by foreign capital inflows, dealers said.
The leu ended trading at about 7,050/100 to the dollar and banks were selling their surpluses to the central bank at those levels, dealers said.
They said the bank supported the current level to prevent the leu from firming that could hurt exports.
"The market should stay dollar-heavy with the central bank soaking up surplus greenbacks to keep exports competitive," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Bucharest.

Operators said the market was expected to remain stable in the coming weeks. They said that even though the leu might come under pressure due to falling money market rates, continuing foreign inflows into Romanian securities would support it.
"Romanian stocks and securities arouse great interest from foreigners, triggering large dollar inflows," said one trader.
Operators said BNR dollar purchases helped the bank to increase its reserves while keeping the money market liquid.

Earlier this week the BNR said its foreign exchange reserves hit $1.45 billion at end-April after dollar purchases from the local market and the restoration last month of International Monetary Fund credits to Romania.
Short-term prices hovered near 103 percent on Friday on a money market. Lower rates were expected in coming weeks on the heels of lower inflation figures for April.
"With becalmed inflation foreign investors should be increasingly attracted to Romania," said another dealer.
On Friday, the National Statistics Board said inflation eased to 6.9 percent in April after an all-time high of 30.7 percent in March when fuel, energy and food prices were freed.
Most traders were confident inflation would fall this summer despite an expected quickening in inflation in May in response to higher gas and heating prices to meet world levels.
"Inflation will pick up this month but we will enjoy a clear decline afterwards. It's difficult to give a figure but you can feel the trend," said one dealer.
Leu retail prices, usually the most sensitive in anticipating further moves, kept to levels of 6,800/7,000 to the dollar of recent weeks.
